Subject: Request: tenant provenance matrix + wipe SLA details

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and compliance team is running through a dedicated-deployment checklist for the pilot. Two quick asks we need clarified before procurement signs off:

1) A simple matrix showing where tenant data can and cannot exist (primary nodes, backups, snapshots, third-party object stores) for a US-dedicated deployment. We need to see whether any cross-region replication or offsite copies are possible by default.

2) Exact observable evidence + timeline for a tenant wipe: what steps are taken, whether snapshots are retained, how long assets persist in backups, and a measurable SLA for complete logical/physical wipe.

If you have a short matrix and any runbook excerpts you can share, that would be ideal. We can treat parts of this as NDA-protected; point me to any links or artifacts and we’ll schedule a follow-up review.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Request: tenant provenance matrix + wipe SLA details

Hi Amir — appreciate the clear asks. High level answers here and I’ve attached a compact provenance matrix plus our SLA excerpt and an ops runbook excerpt for wipe procedures. See the attached files: location-provenance-matrix.xlsx, retention-sla.pdf, ops-wipe-runbook.pdf.

Quick summary:
- Dedicated (US) deployment: primary compute, ephemeral KV caches, and tenant runtime data remain in the pinned cluster (no cross-region replication by default). Backups/snapshots are stored in the same region unless cross-region replication is explicitly configured under an add-on (and that requires explicit customer opt-in and contract).
- Snapshots: automated daily snapshots are retained for the configured retention window (default 30 days). Snapshots are logically tenant-scoped and cannot be rehydrated onto other tenants.
- Wipe process: our standard tenant purge workflow runs in three phases (logical deletion, snapshot sweep, storage reclamation). Measurable targets: logical deletion acknowledged within 1 hour of initiation; snapshot purge started within 24 hours and completed within 72 hours under normal conditions. We provide a wipe completion manifest and audit log entries.

Can Ben and Laura confirm the snapshot sweep and escrow timeline language below — I pulled this from the ops runbook but wanted ops+legal eyes on the wording before we ship back to Amir.

Thanks — attaching the files now.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Request: tenant provenance matrix + wipe SLA details

Vanessa / Laura — quick internal notes (ops):

- Confirmation: By default there is no cross-region replication for Dedicated customers. If a customer purchases the cross-region replication add-on, replicas are stored encrypted with a customer-managed KEK option; we document the regions used in the contract.
- Snapshots: daily, tenant-scoped, stored on region-local object storage. Snapshot chain: full + incremental. Retention window can be set per-customer; default 30 days, max 365 with enterprise agreement.
- Wipe timing nuance: the 72-hour window is for the snapshot purge job to finish under normal operations. For large datasets (multi-TB), the purge is chunked and may take longer; in those cases we provide an in-progress purge manifest and expected ETA.
- Escrow/forensic copy: we do not keep escrow copies beyond retention unless the customer requests a legal hold (and we will document and bill for the extended hold).

Suggested wording tweak for the customer-facing line about evidence: "A wipe completion manifest and audit log entries (including snapshot IDs and object storage delete markers) will be provided within 24 hours of purge job completion."

Ben
Director, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

Amir — following up with the consolidated artifacts and clarified language per our ops review. Key points summarized below and please see the attached matrix and runbook excerpts for the full traceability map: 

- Location: All runtime compute, KV caches, and tenant-specific volumes remain in the pinned US cluster for your Dedicated deployment. Default backup/snapshot storage is also region-local. Cross-region replication only occurs with an explicit add-on and customer opt-in.
- Snapshots & backups: Tenant-scoped; cannot be restored into another tenant. Default retention: 30 days (customer configurable). Chain: periodic full + incremental snapshots; metadata stored with immutable snapshot IDs.
- Wipe workflow & evidence: Initiation -> logical deletion (1 hour) -> snapshot purge job (started within 24 hours) -> storage reclamation (complete within 72 hours under normal load). For very large datasets we provide an ETA and incremental purge manifests. Post-wipe deliverables: wipe-completion-manifest.csv, snapshot-id list, and audit-log export link (S3 pre-signed URL or Drive link).

What I’ve attached: location-provenance-matrix.xlsx (shows compute/storage/backup locations & default behavior), retention-sla.pdf (SLA excerpt with retention/restore limits), ops-wipe-runbook.pdf (redacted runbook excerpt showing purge steps and audit samples).

Next steps: if this covers your needs we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk the matrix and provide sample audit lines. If you want legal/contract language for the purchase order, loop in your procurement and we’ll provide contract wording around region pinning and retention options.

Best regards,
